lifecycle.origin: Created 2026-08-18 by KERNEL_BUILDER-20260818-130753 under the Operator directive that no PostgreSQL or SQLite dependency OR LANGUAGE may remain in tests and checks. Measured during MT-128 implementation: the pg_proof_support fixture conversion REMOVED run_fixture_sql, leaving hard-broken call sites in test_stage_interop.rs (6), test_calendar_interop.rs (6), and test_flight_recorder_authz.rs (1) — those binaries cannot compile. Beyond the compile breaks, ~80 frontend test files still carry PostgreSQL/psql/PG-DSN language in comments, helper names, env-var lists, and gated-row wording, and the shared fixture directory itself is named pg_proof_support. test_e7_swarm_edit_proof.rs was already fully ported under MT-128 (its own scope) and is the reference conversion.

scope.summary: Port the remaining frontend test-suite direct-store verification to embedded-SurrealDB-era patterns and purge PostgreSQL/SQLite language from the frontend test tree. SurrealDB is the canonical main database. CROSS-FILE NOTE: renaming the MT-074 test mt074-op01-save-persists-exact-embed-provenance-in-postgresql must also update the comment referencing it at src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs:755. The reference conversion is test_e7_swarm_edit_proof.rs as ported under MT-128: live-phase row verification goes through product HTTP APIs (documents load, /workspaces list, /workspaces/{id}/loom/blocks/{block}/backlinks, /kernel/events/aggregates/{type}/{id}, credentialed /events); crash-path verification becomes containment observation (the per-run embedded store under a fixture-owned runtime root cannot leak into other runs); shared-cluster sweeps are retired as out-of-band ledger mutation. The pg_proof_support directory is renamed to backend_proof_support with all module references updated across every consuming binary in one change. Operator-approved scope widening adds only the typed calendar source/event ingestion and Atelier intake-item creation API paths needed to replace fixture writes without introducing a generic query backdoor.
forbidden_paths: src/backend/** except the exact allowed paths above

acceptance_criteria.text: Every former run_fixture_sql call site is ported to a product-API or containment-observation proof of EQUIVALENT strength (no assertion is weakened or deleted to make a binary compile), and every affected binary compiles.

No file under src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/ contains PostgreSQL, psql, SQLite, PG-DSN, or PL/pgSQL language — identifiers, env-var names, comments, log strings, or module names — except where a string is a deliberate forbidden-technology tripwire whose purpose is detection.
The pg_proof_support module is renamed database-neutrally and every consuming binary's imports are updated in the same change; git history preserves the rename.

The ported binaries' previously-passing tests still pass on the pinned toolchain (run per binary with --test-threads=1 and the sweep run-configuration lessons from MT-108/MT-127: HANDSHAKE_GPU_SCREENSHOT=1 where pixel rows exist, per-binary scoped HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR isolation).

proof_targets: PT-140-1: repo-wide scan output proving zero PostgreSQL/SQLite language matches under the frontend test tree (tripwire exceptions enumerated).
PT-140-2: per-binary test results for test_stage_interop, test_calendar_interop, test_flight_recorder_authz and every other touched binary, green on the pinned toolchain.

scope.risk_if_missed: Broken binaries silently hold AC-108-3 red; forbidden PostgreSQL language survives in the proof surface the Operator ordered purged; and the next implementer re-diagnoses the removed fixture method from scratch.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Test-harness port; the UI surfaces these tests exercise are owned and proven by their own microtasks.

target_entries: Calendar API module documentation for typed source/event ingestion
expected_evidence: The no-context model manual names the new Atelier intake-item write route.
Calendar module documentation explains typed SurrealDB-backed ingestion and rejects generic query access.

risks: A port that replaces an exact-row SQL assertion with a weaker HTTP existence check silently reduces proof strength (AC-140-1 exists to catch this).
A blanket find/replace of the module name could corrupt string literals that are deliberate tripwires.
Deleting a broken call site instead of porting it converts a canonical-row proof into no proof.
A generic query or test-only mutation endpoint would recreate the direct-store backdoor under a new name.
A non-idempotent import endpoint could duplicate calendar or Atelier records after an ambiguous retry.
Concurrent work already modifies the widened backend files; a broad rewrite could overwrite inherited changes.
minimum_controls: Each replacement proof maps 1:1 to the SQL predicate it replaces and is recorded in PT-140-3.
Tripwire strings that hunt forbidden technology are preserved and enumerated.
No assertion may be deleted without a recorded equivalent.
The widened APIs accept typed domain requests only and call existing SurrealDB-backed stores; no raw query text is accepted.
Caller-stable identities and existing store upsert semantics make retry behavior deterministic.
All edits to inherited-dirty files are surgical and reviewed against the target-specific pre-existing diff.

scope_widening_decision_2026_08_26.operator_quote: approved, surrealdb is the main db. rewrite all older assumption to the new when you come across it. continue work
scope_widening_decision_2026_08_26.effect: Authorizes the minimum backend product API and manual changes needed to replace MT-140's remaining direct-store fixture writes, and authorizes rewriting encountered PostgreSQL/SQLite-era assumptions to SurrealDB-era product terminology. SurrealDB is canonical; no generic database-query surface is authorized.

patterns_found: Typed HTTP setup paths should call existing domain storage methods instead of exposing raw query execution.
Caller-supplied stable external event identities make retry/import behavior idempotent and avoid duplicates after ambiguous failures.
Calendar source and event writes should be workspace-scoped, validate source ownership, and preserve RFC 5545-style stable identities.
Axum routes can be tested through the real Router/HTTP surface; this MT retains its existing live-product proof topology.
reuse_opportunities: Reuse CalendarSourceUpsert, CalendarEventUpsert, normalize_calendar_sync_event, and the existing SurrealDB-backed Storage methods.
Reuse AtelierStore::add_intake_item and NewIntakeItem instead of creating a second ingestion store path.
Reuse the frontend backend_proof_support live server and isolated embedded-store containment.
rejected_options: Generic raw-query, admin-SQL, or test-only fixture endpoints: rejected because they recreate an unsafe storage backdoor and weaken product-level proof.
Keeping legacy DSN helpers under neutral names: rejected because it preserves the obsolete dependency rather than remediating it.
Deleting assertions or substituting fixture success with existence-only checks: rejected because AC-140-1 requires equivalent proof strength.
research_basis.selected_approach: Add only typed workspace-scoped calendar source registration and typed Atelier batch-item creation routes, backed by existing SurrealDB domain stores. Reuse the existing calendar_sync workflow through /jobs for event ingestion and updates; do not add a parallel event-write endpoint. Port tests to those routes/workflow or isolated-store containment, then remove obsolete direct-store helpers and terminology.
mitigations: Stable caller identities and existing upsert semantics
Typed request structs with no query-text field
Surgical patches reviewed against target-specific pre-existing diffs
research_basis.validation_plan: Run focused backend route/store tests, scan the complete frontend test tree with deliberate tripwires enumerated, execute every touched frontend test binary separately with --test-threads=1 and isolated HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR, then perform independent adversarial and counterfactual review.
